items: The Beatles' first UK single, “Love Me Do”, was released on 5 October 1962.
Tickets for the first Glastonbury Festival in 1970 cost £1, and included free milk from the farm.
Live Aid, on 13 July 1985, was held at Wembley Stadium and in Philadelphia at the same time.
A standard piano has 88 keys: 52 white and 36 black.
MTV launched on 1 August 1981. The first video it played was “Video Killed the Radio Star” by The Buggles.
ABBA won the 1974 Eurovision Song Contest in Brighton with “Waterloo”.
Beethoven kept composing after losing his hearing, including his Ninth Symphony.
The Cavern Club in Liverpool, where The Beatles played regularly, opened in 1957.
Mozart was composing music by the age of five.
The Proms have been held at the Royal Albert Hall since 1941.
Orchestras usually tune to an A played by the oboe.
Queen's “Bohemian Rhapsody” was the UK Christmas number one in 1975 and again in 1991.
The Beatles' last public performance was on the roof of Apple Corps in London on 30 January 1969.
Band Aid's “Do They Know It's Christmas?” was recorded on 25 November 1984.
